key_insight: Rapids co-designs a streaming neural decoder with FPGA hardware to deliver accurate, sub-microsecond quantum error correction.
engineering_relevance: Scaling classical decoding hardware alongside qubits offers a path to faster, more accurate fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: Build the neural decoder from FPGA-efficient operations.
Train using the hardware’s integer arithmetic.
Scale across multiple FPGAs or harden into custom silicon.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports under 1 microsecond per syndrome round for a distance-19 surface code on one FPGA, a 240-fold lower logical error rate than existing real-time hardware decoders, and 16-fold better accuracy than Relay on the [[144,12,12]] bivariate-bicycle code.
watch_item: Multi-FPGA deployment must manage communication overhead while preserving throughput and low decision latency.
paper_title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
